inclusion.I1: English language empirical studies with original data
inclusion.I2: Functional MRI scan conducted while human participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task
inclusion.I3: Sample- humans of any age that were either healthy participants, substance users, as well as groups with other neuropsychiatric conditions

exclusion.E1: Studies using only PET or other non-fMRI neuroimaging methods

inclusion.I4: Functional MRI scan conducted while human participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task
inclusion.I5: At least one within-task or between-task contrast related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (e.g., “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “risk > certainty”, “riskier > surer” or “experimental task (risk) > control task” for risky-DM studies; “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”, “ambiguity > ignorance”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous” or “ambiguous task > control task” for ambiguous-DM studies; and “hard > easy”, “low coherence > high coherence”, or “perceptual task > control task” for perceptual-DM studies.
inclusion.I6: Whole-brain evidence- The target analysis must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map
inclusion.I7: It is acceptable for qualifying whole-brain results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials, as long as they are clearly described in the text.

exclusion.E3: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no whole-brain results.
exclusion.E4: Studies that report only seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents) without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map.
exclusion.E5: Studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions (e.g., subgroup vs subgroup, patient vs control) without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain task effect.
exclusion.E6: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original fMRI data in healthy adults.

inclusion.GLOBAL_I2: Whole-brain evidence- Must be a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map

exclusion.GLOBAL_E2: Seed-based connectivity, effective connectivity (e.g., PPI, DCM), or resting-state analyses (e.g., ICA, PLE, Hurst exponents)

inclusion.COMMON_DM_I1: contrasts related to risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making
inclusion.COMMON_DM_I2: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

inclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_I1: contrasts related to ambiguous decision-making (e.g., “ambiguous > certain”, “high-ambiguity > low-ambiguity”, “uncertain > certain” or “experimental task (ambiguity) > control task” for ambiguous-DM studies)
inclusion.AMBIGUOUS_DM_I2: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

inclusion.PERCEPTUAL_DM_I1: contrasts related to perceptual decision-making (e.g., “perceptual > control”, “high-perceptual > low-perceptual” or “experimental task (perceptual) > control task” for perceptual-DM studies)
inclusion.PERCEPTUAL_DM_I2: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

inclusion.RISKY_DM_I1: contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “risk > certainty”, “riskier > surer” or “experimental task (risk) > control task” for risky-DM studies)
inclusion.RISKY_DM_I2: all populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, drug users, patients with substance use disorders, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)

inclusion.NON_USING_RISKY_I1: contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “risk > certainty”, “riskier > surer” or “experimental task (risk) > control task” for risky-DM studies)
inclusion.NON_USING_RISKY_I2: non-substance using populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, or other neuropsychiatric conditions) compared to substance using populations (e.g., drug users, patients with substance use disorders)

inclusion.USING_RISKY_I1: contrasts related to risky decision-making (e.g., “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “risk > certainty”, “riskier > surer” or “experimental task (risk) > control task” for risky-DM studies)
inclusion.USING_RISKY_I2: substance using populations (e.g., drug users, patients with substance use disorders) compared to non-substance using populations (e.g., healthy controls, non-users, or other neuropsychiatric conditions)
